problem: Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}$, ${c}_{2}={b}_{3}$ and ${c}_{3}=-{b}_{2}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Writing a Three-Dimensional Vector in a Different Basis
examples.problem: Let $\mathcal{B}= \left\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2,\mathbf{b}_3 \right\}$ be a basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/1e4b0e4345ef6d0bd0b350cc973eaa7c15b654e76b06cd6f42740af0ab8fc877.png) What are the coordinates of $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}= \left\{ \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2, \mathbf{c}_3 \right\},$ where $\mathbf{c}_1 = -3\mathbf{b}_2,$ $\mathbf{c}_2=-\mathbf{b}_3,$ and $\mathbf{c}_3 = -4\mathbf{b}_1?$
examples.worked_solution:
Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/a5e125038beb90ff4fd2b16bea5b08f83855c80f2a70a73ccfc15fa53fd45a30.png) we can write $\mathbf{x}$ in terms of the vectors $\mathbf c_1, \mathbf c_2,$ and $\mathbf c_3,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}+5{b}_{3} \\  & =-3{b}_{2}+5{b}_{3}-2{b}_{1} \\  & =(-3{b}_{2})-5(-{b}_{3})+\frac{1}{2}(-4{b}_{1}) \\  & ={c}_{1}-5{c}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14065354/assets/f78654ee0612c6daa7e7a1fa26fb56ce0c3c94f6a7ba29805a569eac643946eb.png)

feedback.problem: Let $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}},$ where ${b}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2}$ and ${b}_{2}=-{c}_{1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, we can write $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\  & ={c}_{2}+2{c}_{1} \\  & =2(\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2})-2(-{c}_{1}) \\  & =2{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
